hook_text: One drawing, three faces, every edge measurable. Here is how your sketch becomes something you can actually build.
clip_script: Three lines from one corner: straight up, 30 degrees left, 30 degrees right. Anything parallel to those is true to scale; anything else you find from its ends. Pick a scale so it fits the page, 1 to 2 for a lunch box, 1 to 10 for a drain guard. Draw a faint box the size of your object, nine lines. Then carve: count along the edges to place the rib, the slot, the lip. Darken the real edges. Want to show the inside? Cut a quarter away, or float the lid up the vertical axis. Circles become ovals touching the middles of their square. Slopes come from joining the ends. Then dimensions in real millimetres, never drawing sizes, and notes in capitals: the material, the fold lines, the force the rib fights. If it is not drawn or noted, it will not get built.
visual_style: Grid sheet; three axes flash from one corner; a faint box appears, a container is carved from it, the lid floats up; a circle on a tilted face squashes into an ellipse; dimension lines and capital notes snap on.
pacing: Axes, scale, box, carve, inside views, ellipses and slopes, dimensions and notes.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw your solution's bounding box on a grid sheet tonight.
